claims.text: Machine-learning-guided multi-objective optimization can identify refractory HEA compositions with simultaneously high strength, significant ductility, and reduced weight.
The ML-designed compositions will outperform traditionally selected compositions in strength, ductility, and weight.
Conventional RHEA compositions are determined using trial-and-error or thermo-kinetic approaches.
An ML pipeline integrated with high-throughput simulations can rapidly screen and optimize compositions against strength, ductility, and weight targets.
Optimized elemental ratios mediate the resulting microstructure and phase distribution.
Lattice distortion and solid-solution effects are relevant structural features of the optimized alloys.
An ML model trained on thermo-kinetic and simulation data can capture nonlinear relationships among composition, interatomic bonding, phase stability, and mechanical properties.
The ML model can identify optimal trade-offs among alloying elements.
Rationally optimized compositions can produce microstructures that enhance dislocation mobility and therefore ductility.
Enhanced dislocation mobility can be achieved without compromising alloy strength.
Composition optimization can reduce overall alloy density.
ML-optimized alloys will have a higher strength-to-weight ratio than baseline compositions.
ML-optimized alloys will have greater ductility than baseline compositions.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the ML training data.
Extreme refractory-element concentrations or unforeseen secondary phases may lie outside the ML model's predictive capability.
Experimental RHEA behavior can diverge from simulation predictions.
Experimental fabrication and mechanical testing are necessary to validate the simulation-based predictions.
